topics.title: What Happened to Funko Pop? The Year It Paid to Destroy Its Own Toys
topics.hook: In 2023 the company behind Funko Pop decided to throw away tens of millions of dollars of its own figures.
topics.angle: Start on a shelf of Funko Pops. The collector boom, then too many figures: year-end 2022 inventory of $246.4M (up 48%), warehouses so full it rented containers, and a $30–36M write-down of figures approved for destruction (its own 10-K). Where it is now: 2025 net sales of $908.2M, down from about $1.05B. The lesson: a collectible needs scarcity, a factory needs volume.
topics.why_now: First topics (advice.md: example title 'What Happened to Funko Pop?'). Viewers group it with Labubu (~4 mentions).

topics.title: The Beanie Baby Bubble: When a $5 Toy Was a Retirement Plan
topics.hook: In 1998, a bean bag that cost five dollars made one man more money than Mattel and Hasbro combined.
topics.angle: Open on a bin of Beanie Babies in an attic. Ty Warner's 1998: sales past $1.4 billion on a toy wholesaling at $2.50, retirements and hangtag rumours turning kids' toys into 'investments', eBay's early years riding on them; then the crash, ending with a 2010 auction where 500 of them went for under $100. Close with the same pattern in later blind-box crazes (how it went outside the US: the Canadian distributor's $80M+ a year).

topics.title: Gillette's Ad Got the Blame. P&G's Filing Blamed Your Face

demand.title: Gillette Is (Finally) Getting What They Deserve...

topics.hook: In July 2019, Procter and Gamble wrote eight billion dollars off one razor brand.
topics.angle: Open on a razor cartridge in a bathroom. The best-known razor in the world, the blade-and-handle model, then the 2019 'We Believe' ad and the boycott calls everyone remembers. Then the document device: P&G's own reason for the $8.0B writedown (Reuters, 30 Jul 2019): currency, competition from Dollar Shave Club and Harry's, and men shaving less often; grooming sales down in 11 of 12 quarters. The cause wasn't the ad, it was the beard and the $9 subscription razor. Global beat: currency hit outside the US. Attribute the ad backlash to reporting, the writedown reasons to P&G.
topics.why_now: Breakout: 653K on a 10.8K channel (60x), the strongest English brand-backlash outlier in the scan; brand backlash is a recipe gap (29% hits, one channel posting it).

topics.title: How Toys R Us Lost to Its Own Loan

demand.title: KFC Won the World. So Why Is It Losing America?

topics.hook: Toys R Us was paying about 400 million dollars a year in interest before it sold a single toy.
topics.angle: Open on the giraffe and an empty store. The 2005 buyout by KKR, Bain Capital and Vornado for $6.6B left about $5B of debt and roughly $400M a year in interest; Chapter 11 in September 2017 with about 1,600 stores; in March 2018 the court asked to sell off all 735 US stores, with up to 33,000 jobs. Amazon was the weather; the loan was the leak.

topics.title: Why Everyone Stopped Buying Crocs (and Then Didn't)
topics.angle: Open on a pair of Crocs. The craze to 2007 ($847.4M sales), the crash in 2008 (sales $721.6M, a $185.1M loss, staff cut from about 5,300 to 3,700, a going-concern warning in its own 10-K), and the comeback to about $4.04B in 2025. What changed: the same 'ugly' shoe sold as a canvas (charms, collaborations) instead of a fad. Chapter 1: one model, the Beach, in six colours, launched in 2002 for water sports; the Croslite formula kept as a trade secret.
